01.q: How much does a website or web app cost?
01.a: A contained website costs {essentialRange}; larger websites, web apps and stores sit in higher published ranges. Scope and complexity set the range; content, brand readiness and timeline adjust it. Integrations and performance targets are confirmed with you in scope review, and the proposal fixes one figure.

02.a: No hidden fees. All figures exclude VAT at {vatRate}%. Renewals, paid third-party tools and channels like SMS are billed only if your scope actually uses them, and a maintenance plan is billed, monthly or yearly, only if you choose one.

03.q: What does the payment schedule look like?
03.a: Three payments: {paymentStart} to start, {paymentMilestone} at {milestoneTrigger}, and {paymentFinal} before production launch. Invoices are in EGP for clients in Egypt and in USD for international clients. Code, designs and accounts pass to you at final payment.

04.q: Can I extend the build later?
04.a: Yes. Sign-in, payments or dashboards can be added later as their own scoped change. Each addition is priced from the same published ranges and agreed in writing before work starts.

05.q: Do you work with early-stage companies?
05.a: Yes. Builds start from {minimumEngagement}, for companies that need custom work before they need a large system. Larger systems can be built in phases, so the cost follows the stage of the business.

06.q: Is the proposal price fixed? What if the scope changes?
06.a: The proposal figure is binding for the agreed scope and stays valid for {proposalValidityDays} days. A change to scope is documented and agreed in writing before work on it starts, and priced from the same published ranges. Revision work beyond the included rounds is billed at {revisionRate} per hour.

07.q: Are hosting, a domain and business email included?
07.a: Each is its own line, never folded into the build figure. Hosting is set up and the build deployed to production at launch. Paid third-party services are billed only when your build uses them, and the accounts pass to you at final payment.

08.q: Why not a template or a website builder?
08.a: If a template fits your needs, it costs less and is the right choice. A custom build is worth it when your requirements go beyond one: your own workflows, integrations, every language with proper right-to-left, or performance targets. You also own the source code, the documentation and the accounts.
